event: He leaves the old man's fire before dawn; the old man is asleep, or pretending to be.
The fire was tended in the night. It is always tended.
Link eats an apple in the dark, checks the Slate, and walks north toward the mountain.
Halfway up the northern slope the air changes in a line, and a chill presses on his face.
His breath clouds; grass gives way to frost, frost to rock, rock to ankle-deep snow.
His fingers stiffen, his jaw clenches, and numbness climbs from his toes.
The Slate's hearts dim by a quarter, warmth drained by the air itself.

changes.note: The mountain's cold drains a quarter-heart

event: He pulls the old man's doublet from his pack and on, and the cold is held back, narrowly.
In the lee of a rock shelf he cooks the last three spicy peppers over a fire.
The Slate: Spicy Sauteed Peppers, hearts +3, cold resistance level 1 for 6:30.

changes.note: Spicy Sauteed Peppers, +3 hearts: back to his full 3

event: Doublet outside, peppers inside: he stamps out the fire and climbs on.
Crunch, sink, pull, step: his calves burn, and the thin cold air works his lungs.
A mountain wind drives snow sideways; he climbs toward the amber shrine glow above.
The shrine is half-buried in a drift; he brushes the pedestal clear and sets the Slate.
Inside it is warm and humid, with water running in carved channels and basins.
This transfer feels like structure: water surfaces are no longer just wet, but potential.
The Slate: rune acquired, Cryonis. Create a pillar of ice from a water surface.

changes.note: Link acquires the Cryonis rune in Keh Namut Shrine

event: He aims at a pool, and a clean rectangular pillar of ice cracks up out of the water.
He climbs it and stands on top, and the ice holds him the way stone does.
The cold that drained him outside is now his building material.
He crosses a water gap on three pillars; a fourth makes the first crack and slide away.
He raises a pillar under a half-sunk gate and ducks beneath it on its column of ice.
A pillar in a channel stops the flow, the gears halt, and the platform settles for him.
The third monk waits; he walks to it knowing what will come.
The words arrive, the same as before: the promise of a hero.
He watches the face become light until the platform is empty, and does not look away.
The Slate: Keh Namut Shrine, Cryonis Trial. Spirit Orb acquired, 3/4.

changes.note: Spirit Orb from Keh Namut Shrine: 3/4

event: The mountain's cold crashes back as he rises, and the pepper warmth in his chest is fading.
The southern face is thigh-deep in drifts; his legs burn, and his stamina feels finite.
The cold loosens as he descends: snow to frost to dew, and birds call past the treeline.
The lowland is warm; he opens the doublet's collar, and his clenched body lets go.
In a pine stand by a stream, two red-skinned creatures grunt over a pile of mushrooms.
He pulls a metal shield off their weapon rack with Magnesis, and its clatter confuses them.
He draws the Traveler's Sword, and the fight among them is brief, clean and efficient.
A bow of wood and cord hangs from a post; he tests its draw, and his body knows bows.
He slings it beside the Guardian Sword and takes a quiver of ten or twelve arrows.

changes.note: Link takes the Traveler's Bow and a quiver from the camp

event: The second creature throws a rock; he closes, and the Traveler's Sword rings thin and wrong.
A hairline crack runs up the blade from the tang; it has been forming for days.
He sheathes it carefully and draws the Guardian Sword: twenty attack against its five.
The fourth shrine sits on a bluff at the Plateau's western edge, warm and green.
Slate on pedestal, chime, descent, trial, monk: the pattern has become liturgy.
The strangest transfer yet: things gain yellow-shimmering edges, things that can be paused.
The Slate: rune acquired, Stasis. Freeze an object in time.

changes.note: Link acquires the Stasis rune in Owa Daim Shrine

event: A boulder rolls at him down a track; he points the Slate, and it stops dead, glowing yellow.
He walks past; three seconds later it rolls on, unaware of the gap in its time.
He wonders how long his own gap was, in the basin, in the blue water.
He freezes a metal cube on a seesaw and strikes it five times, its arrow going yellow to red.
Released, the cube flies into the far wall, and the seesaw throws him up to the next ledge.
He freezes a cycling platform at its apex and sprints across in three seconds.
No machine in the last chamber, only the monk; before it he pauses and lets the silence hold.
The words, a fourth time; now he hears beneath them: I waited for you.
The monk dissolves. The Slate: Owa Daim Shrine, Stasis Trial. Spirit Orb acquired, 4/4.

changes.note: Spirit Orb from Owa Daim Shrine: 4/4

event: Four gifts, four people who spent ten thousand years preparing to end. He carries them all.
On the path to the summit he tries Stasis on a lone creature: nothing. Only objects.
Prying a wedged stone from the path, the Traveler's Sword snaps clean along its crack.
He turns the hilt over, its leather worn to his hand, and tucks it in his belt anyway.
Even the things he trusts have a shelf life. He draws the Guardian Sword and climbs.
Mount Hylia's peak is a narrow, wind-scoured ridge, and the cold cuts through to the bone.
His legs shake, his fingers are numb, his face raw; standing in the wind is work.
Below: the fire mountain, the dark castle, twin peaks over a river valley, lakes in the light.
He can name things now: the temple, the abbey, the cabin's smoke, four dimmed shrines.
The Plateau looks small, a garden outgrown in four days, and its edge is a door now.
Beyond it, everything. He stands until the wind makes his eyes water, then descends.
The old man's fire is burning, and he stands beside it, tense, as Link comes through the grass.
"You have what I asked for." His voice is steady, but the steadiness is work.
Link stops at the firelight with four orbs, four runes, and a useless hilt in his belt.
"Come to the Temple of Time at dawn. We'll make the trade."
He turns a log a quarter-turn, as always, and his fingers tremble slightly.
Link sits as the warmth finds the summit's cold in his bones, and eats what the old man made.
Four nights by this fire; it feels like a life, the only one he has.
Tomorrow the trade, the paraglider, and the world beyond the edge.
The old man's back is to him, hooded, firelit: a century of patience, allowed to end.
Link closes his eyes. The fire cracks. The stars turn. Tomorrow.
